question: Who among the following started the Satnami movement for the betterment of leather workers in Central India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Guru Ghasidas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Guru Ghasidas was a prominent social reformer and spiritual leader of the Satnami sect in the early 19th century.
 
• The Satnami movement was initiated by Guru Ghasidas for the upliftment of the marginalized and oppressed communities, particularly the leather workers in Central India.
 
• He emphasized the principles of truth, non-violence, and equality, and preached against the caste-based discrimination prevalent in society.
 
• Guru Ghasidas is revered as a significant figure in the history of social reform in India, and his teachings continue to inspire many.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Satnami Movement**

 
 
• The Satnami movement emerged as a significant socio-religious movement in Central India, particularly in the Chhattisgarh region.
 
• It was started by Guru Ghasidas in the early 19th century to challenge the social hierarchies and caste-based discrimination.
 
• The movement emphasized the worship of Satnam (the True Name) and rejected the orthodox practices and rituals of the dominant Brahminical religion.
 
• Satnamis, the followers of the movement, primarily belong to the Dalit community and have a strong presence in Chhattisgarh and neighboring regions.
 
 
 
• **Guru Ghasidas**
 
 
• Guru Ghasidas was born in 1756 in the village of Girodpuri in present-day Chhattisgarh.
 
• He is considered a pioneer of the Satnami sect, which aimed to eradicate social evils and promote equality and justice.
 
• Guru Ghasidas preached the message of truth, unity, and non-violence, and his teachings emphasized the inherent dignity and worth of every individual.
 
• He is remembered for his efforts to uplift the marginalized sections of society and his contribution to the social reform movement in India.
